column1: AFUE vs ThermalEfficiency (why the same number produces different results)
AFUE is an annualized seasonal average and the code applies it as a flat constant across every OAT so the integrated annual efficiency equals the user's entry exactly.

ThermalEfficiency is a steady-state nameplate; the code loads the SystemType's reference OAT polynomial (dfCurve) and only shifts its constant term by (defaultEff - userEff). The curve shape dips at low OAT where OA-reset keeps return water above the condensing dew point so the HDD-weighted integral runs below the entered value.
Example: ThermalEfficiency=0.95 on condGasBoilerOAreset integrates to ~0.89 under Boston TMY (about 6 percentage points below entered). AFUE=0.95 on the same load integrates to 0.95 exactly.

Rule of thumb: use AFUE when you want the entered value to equal the annual effective efficiency. Use ThermalEfficiency only when you want OAT-dependent condensing behavior and accept that the integrated value will differ from the nameplate.
